# Performance & first-paint pass — 25 Oct 2026

Scope: the splash screen, the "FAQs before the hero" flash on the home page and
on volume pages, scroll lag, and the weight of the volume route. Plus the
comparative-evidence merge into Volume 27.

## 1. Splash screen: 10 s → 2 s

`src/components/AscensionSplash.tsx` — the five acts (Calvary → light → the Lord
rises → the declaration → the ascension) are unchanged, but the timeline is now
authored against `SPLASH_SECONDS = 2`:

| Act | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Calvary fade + Ken Burns | 1.4 s / 10.6 s | 0.35 s / 2.0 s |
| Rays, glow, dust | from 0.5 s | from 0.1 s |
| Jesus rises onto screen | 2.3 s | 0.55 s |
| Declaration (title → verse) | 2.3 → 3.8 s | 0.28 → 0.66 s |
| Ascension + beam + flash + dissolve | 5.7 → 9.8 s | 1.15 → 2.0 s |

The 40 ms start beat (was 250 ms) and the failsafe (2 s + 1.5 s) follow the new
duration. Skip still fast-forwards at ×6; `prefers-reduced-motion` fades in ~1.9 s.

## 2. "The FAQs show up first, then the hero banner"

Two independent causes, both fixed.

**(a) A visible FAQ block was injected over the pre-render shell.**
`public/assets/seo-aeo.js` polled `#root` every 150 ms and injected a visible
"Frequently Asked Questions" section as soon as the container had *any* child.
Every client-rendered route ships a crawler-facing block inside `#root`
(`scripts/prerender-seo.mjs`), so the block was painted while the JS bundle was
still downloading — then replaced by the hero. It now waits for React to paint
(`html[data-sp-app="ready"]`, set by `RootLayout`, and the `sp-app-ready` event
from the splash), and only appears on the home route. The FAQ/JSON-LD + GEO head
markup is unchanged.

**(b) The crawler shell itself was painted before the app.**
`index.html` now carries an inline, network-free **boot curtain** in the splash's
own colours (z-index 9998, under the splash). It is removed on `sp-app-ready`
(fallbacks: `load` + 2.5 s, hard 6 s, `noscript` disables it). Result: first
paint is the brand — never a serif list of site links — and cold loads on slow
connections no longer start with a white screen. `public/sw.js` → `sp-pwa-v8`
so returning visitors drop the cached copy of the old retrofit scripts.

## 3. Volume route: one 628 kB chunk → the dossier being read

`src/data/volumes/index.ts` statically imported all 51 `volume_NN.ts` modules, so
**every** volume page downloaded 628 kB (221 kB gzip) before rendering a
paragraph. New `src/data/volumes/registry.ts` loads them with
`import.meta.glob`, so Rollup emits one chunk per volume (7–45 kB).

`VolumePage` now paints immediately from the 82 kB catalogue index
(`volumeIndex.json`): the real hero banner, title, subtitle and CTAs, then the
dossier streams in (`VolumeDossierLoading` holds the height, so there is no
layout shift). Prev/next and related-volume cards read the same lite index.
`VolumeNumberRedirect` also uses the index instead of the full corpus.
The `volumes-data` manualChunk was removed from `vite.config.ts`.

## 4. Other main-thread wins

- **`public/assets/companion.js`** walked *every* `h2,h3,h4,div,span,p` and read
  `.textContent` off each one — several times (300 ms / 1.2 s / 3 s / repaint) —
  on long volume pages. It now targets `#companion-modules` first, scans
  headings only, runs once, and hides (never removes) the React-owned panel.
- **Home-page module iframe** (`ModuleSwitcher`) mounts the 300 kB atlas document
  only when it comes within 500 px of the viewport, with a same-height placeholder.
- **Sticky header blur** is dropped below 768 px (a `position: sticky` backdrop
  filter re-composites every frame while scrolling); a near-opaque tint keeps the
  identical look.
- The server-rendered `/encyclopedia/:slug` article (Vercel function) now
  time-boxes its Firestore round-trip to 600 ms and is edge-cacheable
  (`s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`); `markdownToHtml` learned
  `*italics*` and `> blockquotes`.

## 5. Volume 27 — comparative dossier merged

`scripts/merge_volume_27_evidence.mjs` (idempotent) appends Part VI–VII to
`src/data/volumes/volume_27.ts` — Jewish-scripture passages, the blasphemy
episodes, the historical witnesses (Pliny, Philippians hymn, Sanhedrin 43a,
Najran, Dome of the Rock, John of Damascus, Timothy I, "Two Powers"), where the
evidence cuts the other way, the Quran/hadith material and the framing advice —
plus a new reference table (7 witnesses), 4 FAQ entries and 3 key facts. The
`volumesData.json` mirror is refreshed so `dist/encyclopedia/<slug>.md` and
`llms.txt` carry the same text.

# Saul's Podship

Comparative apologetics and Bible-encyclopedia SPA for [saulspodship.com](https://www.saulspodship.com) —
50+ illustrated volumes, biblical maps atlas, a 400-question comparative codex
(Islam / Judaism / Hinduism / Sikhism), a Pakistani Christian music archive, and
prophecy tools.

**Stack:** React 19 + Vite 6 + TypeScript · Tailwind CSS 4 · Express (served via a
single Vercel function) · Firestore REST API · React Router (`createHashRouter`).

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # dev server on :3000 (tsz server.ts behind gen-volume-index)
```

## Scripts

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Volume index generation + `tsx server.ts` dev server |
| `npm run build` | Link check → `vite build` → postbuild prerender → music prerender → bundles `server.ts` to `dist/server.cjs` |
| `npm start` | Run the built server (`dist/server.cjs`) |
| `npm run lint` | Type-check (`tsc --noEmit`) |
| `npm test` | Hero-variant integrity test (unique MD5s per variant) |
| `npm run test:about` | After building, checks the app directory, FAQs, structured data and crawler output |
| `npm run verify` | Codex integrity gate (`scripts/verify-codex.mjs`, 400/400 cards) |
| `npm run gen:volumes` | Regenerate `src/data/volumes/volumeIndex.json` |
| `npm run gen:i18n` | Emit `public/i18n/*.json` + bundle `public/assets/sp-i18n.js` from `src/data/i18n/` |
| `npm run test:i18n` | Dictionary/coverage/engine gate (also runs inside `npm run build`) |

## Verify before finishing (required)

```bash
npm run lint && npm test && npm run verify && npm run build && npm run test:about
```

## Languages (Urdu / Hindi / Arabic)

The language switcher translates the whole site — React pages, every volume's body text,
tables, timelines, story panels, the Companion bar, the static module docs and the
Comparative Apologetics codex iframe. It is **fully static**: no translation API and no
server round-trip. The dictionary lives in `src/data/i18n/` and is emitted to
`public/i18n/{ur,hi,ar}.json`; English visitors download nothing.

```bash
npm run gen:i18n                          # after editing any dictionary or pattern
node scripts/harvest-i18n.mjs --missing   # which user-facing strings still lack an entry
node scripts/test-i18n-dom.mjs            # optional jsdom end-to-end check (needs `npm i -D jsdom`)
```

Strings built from data (`Vol 12: …`, `Browse 51 Volumes`, `Last Updated: September 6, 2026`,
tab titles) are handled by templated **patterns** in `src/data/i18n/patterns.ts`, so adding a
volume never needs a dictionary edit — and digits are localised too (`۵۱` / `५१` / `٥١`).
Text that is already in the target language is skipped via `translate="no"` /
`data-sp-notranslate` / `.urdu`. To see gaps live: `localStorage['sp-i18n-debug']='1'`
(or `?i18n-debug=1`), then `window.__spI18n.report()`. See `AGENTS.md` → *Language layer*
for the rules.

## About page: public app directory

`src/data/podshipApps.json` is the shared list of verified public subdomain apps. The About page, navigation, FAQ answers, structured data, prerendered HTML and generated `llms.txt` use this list. Add or change a product there only after checking its public URL and official logo. The locally hosted Biblical Languages and Sunday School WebP icons are optimized from their original 192px app icons ([Biblical Languages](https://biblicallanguages.saulspodship.com/icon-192.png), [Sunday School](https://saulssundayschool.saulspodship.com/assets/icons/icon-192.png)); the Evangelism and Biblical Cosmos SVG marks are copies of those projects' original icons. The About and FAQ page text and structured-data helpers live in `src/data/about.ts` and `src/data/faq.ts`. Run the build and `npm run test:about` after changes.

## Repo conventions (read before contributing)

- **`AGENTS.md`** — agent guardrails, incl. the frozen codex artifact rules.
- **`.github/workflows/`** — `videos-sync` refreshes `public/videos/assets/videos-data.*`
  daily (18:15 PKT); `vercel-cleanup` prunes old Vercel deployments on demand.
  **Never hand-edit those generated data files** and don't fight the automation.
- **`main` is the only long-lived branch** (`dev` and the `promote-dev` workflow were
  retired 2026-09-13). Every push to `main` triggers a full production deployment
  (~95 MB build copy each), so batch related changes into one push and merge
  short-lived branches only once they're ready.
- Before committing any new/edited image under `public/`, run
  `python3 scripts/optimize_images.py` (needs Pillow). Never commit multi-MB PNG/JPG.
- Commit as `saulspodship <saulspodship@gmail.com>` — the Vercel-linked account.
  On the Hobby plan with a private repo, Vercel blocks deployments authored by
  any other GitHub account.

# Comparative Apologetics Codex — install package for saulspodship.com

This folder is a **drop-in add-on** for the Saul's Podship Vite + React + Tailwind
site (React Router `createHashRouter`, lucide-react icons, wine `#4A152C` /
gold `#E8C96A` / cream `#F8F4E3` palette).

It adds a **fifth pillar** — "400 Comparative Questions" — to the
*Four Pillars of Saul's Podship* section on the home page, plus a
new route `/comparative-apologetics` that hosts the complete interactive codex
(100 questions each on Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Sikhism).

## What the agent must do (summary — full steps in `.agent/workflows/`)

1. Copy `public/comparative-apologetics/` → project `public/` (static codex HTML, ~1.5 MB).
2. Copy `src/components/pillars/ComparativeApologeticsPillar.jsx`,
   `src/pages/ComparativeApologeticsPage.jsx`,
   `src/data/comparativeApologeticsIndex.json` into the same paths in the project.
3. Register the route `{ path: "comparative-apologetics", element: <ComparativeApologeticsPage /> }`
   in the router **before** the `path: "*"` 404 route.
4. On the home page, insert `<ComparativeApologeticsPillar />` as the **5th card** of the
   pillar grid, directly after the "Tough Questions" card, and change
   `lg:grid-cols-4` → `lg:grid-cols-5` (or `xl:grid-cols-5 lg:grid-cols-3`).
5. Update the section intro text to read "Five Pillars of Saul's Podship".
6. Add `/comparative-apologetics` to the Sitemap page and `sitemap.xml` (if present).
7. Run `npm run build` and confirm `dist/comparative-apologetics/codex.html` exists.

## Hard rules

- **Do not** edit, minify, re-format, or "clean up" `public/comparative-apologetics/codex.html`.
  It is a verified, self-contained document: 400 `article.qcard` elements with stable IDs
  (`q-islam-1` … `q-sikhism-100`), its own CSS/JS toolbar, and tested behaviour.
  Any change there must go through `scripts/verify-codex.mjs` and pass 400/400.
- **Do not** import the codex HTML into the React bundle. It is served as a static asset
  and embedded via `<iframe>` — this is intentional (bundle size, style isolation).
- **Do not** rename the route slug `comparative-apologetics`; `canonical`, JSON-LD and
  deep links (`?q=q-islam-83`, `?rel=hinduism`) depend on it.
- Match the existing pillar card markup exactly (same Tailwind classes) so the fifth card
  is visually identical to the other four. Do not introduce new colours.
- Keep the existing four pillars, their links, and their copy unchanged.
- Preserve `createHashRouter`; do not switch to `createBrowserRouter`.
- **Do not** add a private translation dictionary anywhere (component, `public/assets/*.js`,
  or a static module page). The one dictionary lives in `src/data/i18n/` — see
  [Language layer](#language-layer-sp-i18n). A second copy drifts, and the codex enhancer
  already proved it.
- **Do not** hand-edit the generated i18n artifacts: `public/i18n/{ur,hi,ar}.json`,
  `public/assets/sp-i18n.js`, `src/data/i18n/version.ts`. They are emitted by
  `scripts/build-i18n.mjs` (and rewritten by every `npm run build` / `npm run dev`).

## Language layer (`sp-i18n`)

The site ships Urdu / Hindi / Arabic alongside English. Translation is **static and
client-side only** — no translation API, no server round-trip. The dictionary is bundled
from `src/data/i18n/` into `public/i18n/*.json`; English visitors never download a byte of it.

How it fits together:

| Piece | Path | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dictionary sources (edit these) | `src/data/i18n/dict-{chrome,volumes,pages,modules}.ts` | `[ur, hi, ar]` tuples keyed by the English string |
| Templated rules (edit these) | `src/data/i18n/patterns.ts` | regex → template for strings built from data (`Vol 12: …`, `Browse 51 Volumes`, `Last Updated: …`, tab titles) |
| Emitter | `scripts/build-i18n.mjs` (`npm run gen:i18n`) | writes `public/i18n/*.json`, `src/data/i18n/version.ts`, and bundles `public/assets/sp-i18n.js` |
| Runtime | `src/lib/i18n/{store,engine,react}.ts(x)` | the React translator: `MutationObserver` + per-frame settle passes, `WeakMap` original registry, same-origin iframe walking |
| Fallback runtime | `src/lib/i18n/standalone.ts` → `public/assets/sp-i18n.js` | `window.__spI18n` for static module docs and the codex enhancer; inside a frame it only sets `lang`/`dir`/fonts and defers to the parent |
| Gate | `scripts/test-i18n.mjs` (`npm run test:i18n`) | runs inside `npm run build` — fails on stale artifacts, wrong-script values, empty entries, untranslated chrome/volume/module strings |
| DOM gate (optional) | `scripts/test-i18n-dom.mjs` | jsdom end-to-end proof (needs `npm i -D jsdom`; skips cleanly without it) |
| Coverage audit | `scripts/harvest-i18n.mjs` | scans `src/` for user-facing strings and reports which have no dictionary entry |

Rules when touching UI text:

1. **Prefer a pattern over a dictionary entry for anything built from data.** Volume
   numbers, dates, counts and titles are generated, so a literal entry rots the moment a
   volume is added. Patterns also localise digits (`۵۱` / `५१` / `٥١`).
2. **A new page/volume/module is not done until its strings translate.** Add entries, run
   `npm run gen:i18n`, then check `node scripts/harvest-i18n.mjs --missing`.
3. **Never translate text that is already in the target language.** Mark it
   `translate="no"` or `data-sp-notranslate` (see `TheologicalArchivePage`, and the `.urdu`
   / `.urdu-body` classes the engine always skips).
4. **`codex.html` stays frozen.** It is translated two ways without being edited: the
   parent engine walks its same-origin iframe, and `podship-enhance.js` injects
   `sp-i18n.js` for direct visits.
5. A static module doc gets `<script src="/assets/sp-i18n.js" defer></script>` in `<head>`.
   Keep it to one reference per page — the gate counts them.

Debugging gaps on the live site: `localStorage['sp-i18n-debug']='1'` (or `?i18n-debug=1`)
outlines every untranslated node, and `window.__spI18n.report()` lists the misses.

## Verify before finishing

```bash
node scripts/verify-codex.mjs      # 400 cards, 4×100, unique IDs, toolbar present
npm run build
ls dist/comparative-apologetics/codex.html
```
Then open `/#/comparative-apologetics`, click a religion chip (it filters **and**
scrolls to that section), click a question title (it expands), and change the sort to
"Most asked in Pakistan & India".

## Deployment storage hygiene (Vercel)

Every push to `main` creates a production deployment, and Vercel keeps a FULL copy
of the build output (`dist/`, ~95 MB) for every retained deployment. ~120 pushes in
three weeks is what caused the 11 GB Deployment Storage spike in Sep 2026.

- **`main` is the only long-lived branch.** The `dev` branch and the daily
  `promote-dev` workflow were retired on 2026-09-13 — everything lives in `main`.
  Since every push to `main` is now a production deployment, **batch related
  changes into a single push** rather than pushing after each commit, and do the
  work in short-lived branches that get merged once they are ready.
- Before committing any new or edited image under `public/`, run:
  `python3 scripts/optimize_images.py` (needs Pillow). It compresses in place and
  generates missing `hero-1920.webp` variants. Never commit multi-MB PNG/JPG.
- Keep hero generation settings in `scripts/make_hero_variants.py` at q<=80.
- To reclaim storage: Actions -> "Clean old Vercel deployments" (needs the
  `VERCEL_TOKEN` repo secret); dry-run first. Deletions are restorable 30 days.
- **Git identity:** always commit with
  `user.name = saulspodship` / `user.email = saulspodship@gmail.com` — the GitHub
  account linked to the project's Vercel. The repo is PRIVATE and Vercel is on the
  Hobby plan, so ONLY commits authored by an account with project access deploy;
  anything else is blocked ("Git author ... must have access to the project on
  Vercel"). `111325113+Solatjamil@users.noreply.github.com` resolves to a DIFFERENT
  GitHub account (`Solatjamil`) and its commits were blocked on 2026-09-13 — do not
  use it, even though earlier revisions of this file recommended it.
